MINUTES OF THE REGULAR MEETING
  CITY OF NORWALK PARKS AND RECREATION COMMISSION
  September 10, 2026

Commissioner Anthony Armendarez called the meeting to order at 6:08 p.m.

Commission members present were Anthony Armendarez, Maria Carbajal, Alejandra
Hernandez, Victor Juan, David King, Briana Martinez, Antoinette Moreno, Brian Tindall,
Monique Yanez, and Don Valenzuela.
Staff present included Recreation Superintendent Sonia Batres, Recreation Supervisor
Pati Garcia, Recreation Supervisor Rosie Lozoya, and Office Assistant II Vanessa
Piceno.

APPROVAL OF MINUTES

Commissioner Hernandez motioned to accept the August 13, 2026, meeting minutes.
Commissioner Moreno seconded the motion.
REPORTS

Summer 2026 Programming Re-cap

Recreation Supervisor, Rosie Lozoya, presented a re-cap of the Summer 2026
Recreation and Park Services Programming. The Commission requested for
consideration of installment of more pipe tunnels at the Robert White Dog Parks.

Fall Programming Preview

Recreation Supervisor, Pati Garcia, presented an overview of the Fall 2026 events,
including the Arturo Sanchez Sr Halloween Parade, Halloween Festival, Pumpkin Float,
and Adaptive Recreation Halloween Dance. The Commission recommended that the
department explore opportunities to promote the Halloween Festival on the chain-link
fence at The Walk project development to increase visibility and encourage greater
community participation.

Park Projects Monthly Update

Recreation Superintendent, Sonia Batres, presented an update on current and
upcoming park improvement projects throughout the city. The Commission requested
for updates on Norwalk Park to be added to future meetings.

STAFF COMMENTS

Superintendent Batres provided the Parks and Recreation Commissioners with an
update on Department programs and upcoming events. She provided an update on the

youth advisory body board. The Teen Green initiative will run through April 2027 with
the in collaboration with the Summer Youth Worker Program. There are three remaining
dates for the Lattes and Leashes event: September 12, 19, and 26. Taste and State of
the City will take place on October 16 at 11 a.m. attendees will be able to hear what’s
happening across Norwalk and enjoy delicious food from local vendors.

COMMISISONER’S COMMENTS

Commissioner Yanez – Shared that the Los Alisos fields have not been laser leveled and
requested clarification regarding the budget and the City’s role following the revision of
the contract for fields.

Commissioner Valenzuela – Suggested that the department explore the possibility of
installing a marquee at Norwalk Boulevard and Imperial Highway to help promote citywide
events and programming.

Commissioner Tindall – Asked about the plan for Norwalk Park and whether connecting
the NASC and Aquatic Pavilion parking lots along the freeway wall are included in the
design.

Commissioner Moreno – She raised safety concerns regarding ongoing e-bikes issue.
She also asked about the possibility of looking into more permanent signage inside the
Holifield restrooms to improve cleanliness. The Pony and Bronco fields have limited
availability due to Recreation programming field usage. Fall ball is expected to have
approximately 200–300 players. It was recommended that Recreation consider using
Norwalk Park or other location as an alternative location. A floating lantern festival was
also suggested for consideration.

Commissioner Martinez – Asked about the Youth Advisory Board and which staff would
be overseeing the program.

Commissioner King – Welcomed back Commissioners Juan and Martinez and
recognized the Recreation and Park Services Department for doing a great job with
programs and events.

Commissioner Juan – Reported concerns regarding e-bike issues at Gerdes Park and
noted that Public Safety had been present.

Commissioner Hernandez – Recommended a more extensive discussion regarding e-
bikes and Public Safety, including revisiting the idea of posting park rules to clarify
whether e-bikes are permitted and help prevent confusion regarding park regulations.
She also expressed interest in becoming more connected with teen programming, noting

that these programs could provide a good opportunity to share information about the
commissioner’s roles.

Commissioner Carbajal – Suggested contacting the school safety department regarding
the e-bike concerns as well for additional support at Holifield Park.

Commissioner Armendarez – Welcomed back Commissioners Juan and Martinez and
gave kudos to the department for its recent events. He also expressed excitement about
the upcoming fall events. Regarding the Youth Advisory board, he expressed interest in
receiving additional information and updates as the process continues. He also shared
concerns regarding e-bikes at Holifield Park and inquired about the possibility of adding
Park Pal programming at Glazier Park.

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS
NEXT MEETING
October 8, 2026
There being no further business to discuss, Commissioner Armendarez motioned to
adjourn the meeting. Seconded by Commissioner Juan. All in favor. The meeting was
adjourned at 7:22 p.m.

Respectfully submitted,

__________________________
Chairperson Anthony Armendarez
